results.content:
Gauth vs. Study Genius AI. Study Genius AI is positioned around structured study support rather than one-off problem solving. Where Gauth shines on "I'm stuck right now, explain this," a platform like Study Genius AI is built for ongoing study plans, review schedules, and broader curriculum support. Students cramming for a specific test tonight will get more immediate value from Gauth's speed; students managing an entire semester's worth of material across multiple subjects may prefer a tool built around that longer arc. Pricing transparency also favors Study Genius AI, which publishes a clearer tier structure than Gauth does. [...] Gauth is built for students who hit a wall on a specific problem and need an explanation fast, not for students looking for a structured course or curriculum. If your study pattern looks like "I'm stuck on problem 7, I need to understand why," Gauth's photo-to-solution flow and step-by-step explanations are exactly the right shape of tool.

Gauth fits particularly well for:

Gauth is a weaker fit for students who need sustained, structured learning over weeks, like exam prep built around spaced repetition or a full course curriculum. For that kind of long-horizon studying, a dedicated platform like Study Genius AI may serve better, since Gauth is architected around solving the problem in front of you rather than building a study plan around what you'll need to know next month. [...] The category Gauth competes in sits between pure AI chatbots and dedicated study platforms like Study Genius AI. Where a general chatbot requires you to type out a problem (which is often the hardest part with math notation or diagrams), Gauth's visual input removes that friction entirely. That's the core value proposition: speed from problem to explanation, with minimal setup.

Gauth's feature set centers on four capabilities: photo-to-solution solving, conversational follow-up, multi-agent assignment processing, and source-linked topic research through Atlas. Each targets a different point in a student's workflow, from a single tricky problem to an entire assignment to open-ended research.

results.title: SnapGPT vs Gauth / GauthMath (2026): Which AI Solver Is Better?
results.content:
## Why SnapGPT is the best Gauth alternative

### Built for the browser, not the camera roll

Gauth (formerly GauthMath) is a phone-first app: you photograph a problem, then read the solution on your phone. That's fine for a paper textbook — but most graded homework now lives in Canvas, McGraw Hill Connect, ALEKS, or Google Forms, in a browser. SnapGPT is a browser extension, so the answer arrives on the same page as the question, in one click. And for the homework that is still on paper, the SnapGPT iOS app is coming soon — point your camera at the worksheet, tap Solve, and get the answer with steps and a follow-up chat.

### Every subject, not math-plus [...] ### Pricing

Gauth's free tier is limited and its paid plan runs about $12/month, with human-tutor help priced on top. SnapGPT is free for 5 answers a day, and Plus — unlimited answers, chat, SmartScan, Autopilot — starts at $9.99/month or $89.99/year. See pricing.

## Gauth vs SnapGPT: who should choose what?

### Choose SnapGPT if:

 Your homework and quizzes live in a browser, not on paper
 You take courses beyond math and need every subject covered
 You want one-click answers without a second device
 You want chat, explanations, flashcards, and Autopilot in one tool
 You want a cheaper paid plan with a real free tier

### Choose Gauth if: [...] Does Gauth work on Canvas or other online quiz sites?

Not natively. Gauth is a phone app (with a web upload page), so using it on online quizzes means photographing your screen or copy-pasting questions. SnapGPT is a browser extension that reads the quiz page directly.

  Can SnapGPT solve math like GauthMath?

Yes. SnapGPT uses GPT-5.6 and Claude with vision, so it solves algebra through calculus, reads graphs and diagrams, and renders steps in proper math notation. It also covers chemistry, physics, biology, history, and essay questions — it isn't a math-only tool.

results.content:
A few deserve a closer look. Wolfram Alpha works as an AI math solver that pairs well with graphing tools such as GeoGebra, and Mathway covers similar ground for algebra.

Khan Academy leans on full video lessons instead of quick textbook solutions, suited to rebuilding a subject from scratch. Socratic by Google sits at the other end, built for a fast multi-subject nudge.

ChatGPT or Gemini work more like an open-ended AI study tool, useful for follow-up questions through ongoing AI chat rather than a single scanned answer.

## How Gauth reads a photo and returns an answer

Gauth, formerly GauthMath, is an AI homework helper owned by ByteDance. Students snap a photo of a problem and get an AI-generated answer with step-by-step solutions. [...] | ChatGPT or Gemini | Open-ended explanation and follow-up | Limited daily use | ChatGPT Plus or Google AI Pro, about $20/mo |
| Brainly | Community-sourced homework help | Basic access with ads | Brainly Plus, $9.99/mo or $39.99/yr (US pricing) |
| Nibble | Broader knowledge once homework's done | Limited free access | Nibble Premium, $11.99/mo or $49.99/yr | [...] ### Which app explains math better than Gauth does?

Depends what you need help with. Symbolab digs into more technical step-by-step detail for tougher problems, while Khan Academy builds full lessons around a concept instead of just spitting out an answer. Both go deeper than Gauth typically does, and Khan Academy works especially well if you're relearning a topic from scratch.

### Is Gauth Plus worth paying for, or should I stick with free?

Rarely, if you're an occasional user. Most people never hit the free tier's scan cap, which makes Gauth Plus a hard sell for light use. But scan five or six problems on a bad homework night, and that monthly fee starts looking less like an upsell and more like a fair price for not getting stuck.
